blockers: At native 1x, the torso, hips, and legs collapse into a narrow dark column; the character reads as a blue armored stick figure rather than a clearly structured 5.5-head character.

The idle strip has almost no readable breathing, balance, or weapon-settle motion. The 16 frames appear close to static pose duplicates, so the intended controlled personality is not being communicated.

Locomotion lacks convincing weight transfer. Leg separation and foot placement are too subtle, and several directions read as the same pose with rotated weapon/arms rather than distinct directional gait states.
The face is an overbright white oval with tiny, unstable-looking features. At native scale it has insufficient hairline, jaw, eye, and shadow structure, producing a blank or uncanny mask.
The signature gesture does not establish a strong anticipation, decisive rapier action, overshoot, and settle. The arm and blade changes are too small to read as a deliberate character beat.
The navy-on-black costume loses major form boundaries. Blue highlights are doing most of the modeling, while the corset, high collar, and brass trim are not separated strongly enough at native scale.
high_value_changes: Redesign the silhouette before adding detail: widen and clarify the shoulder/collar mass, separate the forearms from the torso, open the hip-to-leg negative space, and give the rapier hand a cleaner readable contour.

Build a stronger four-to-six-frame locomotion contact cycle with obvious passing, contact, and recovery poses. Keep the ground anchor fixed while moving the pelvis, shoulders, and weapon through a controlled counter-swing.
Push the gesture into a readable arc: compressed anticipation, sharp rapier extension, one-frame overshoot, then a restrained return and visible blade settle.
Reserve near-black for recesses and use a distinct mid-value navy for the corset and skirt/leg masses. Add a small, consistently placed brass accent that survives 1x viewing.
Replace the featureless face with a simplified pixel face: controlled hair silhouette, one stable eye line, a readable shadow under the collar or chin, and fewer high-value white pixels.
Audit every direction at native size using a silhouette-only pass. Each direction must preserve head, shoulder, hip, foot, and blade readability without relying on color highlights.
optional_notes: The 119.8px measured height and zero anchor drift satisfy the stated technical contract; those are not the current quality risks.
The 4x nearest-neighbor enlargement exposes soft-rendered or gradient-heavy modeling that is less convincing when inspected as discrete native pixels.
The rapier provides the strongest secondary silhouette cue, but its angle and visibility vary enough across directions that it cannot currently carry the full read.
The character is vertical and contained, but the current restraint has become visual inactivity rather than controlled poise.
regressions_from_previous: No prior-round visual sheet or metric comparison was supplied, so specific regressions from round-21 cannot be verified.

Current-round risk to monitor against the previous version: increased reliance on dark gradients and tiny facial highlights may have reduced native-scale form separation even if the enlarged render appears more polished.
strongest_improvements: Standing height remains within the 128px limit.
Ground anchoring is stable with 0px measured drift.
The blue-black and brass concept is coherent, and the rapier gives the otherwise narrow figure a useful directional accent.
The eight-direction sheet maintains a broadly consistent character design across viewpoints.
luna_evaluation.single_most_important_next_change: Rebuild the native 1x silhouette and locomotion poses together, prioritizing clear shoulder-to-hip structure, separated legs and feet, and an unmistakable weight-transfer cycle before refining palette or facial detail.
